fsm_overview: Annex C of the spec defines six normative FSMs covering the I3C Bus lifecycle: Main Master, Slave Interrupt Request, Dynamic Address Assignment, Hot-Join, Secondary Master Request, Master Regaining Bus Ownership, plus an I2C Legacy Master sub-FSM.

fsm_states.name: IDLE
fsm_states.description: Bus free / available; SDA and SCL both HIGH (released, optional High-Keeper); no transaction active. Master may initiate a new frame; Slaves may issue Hot-Join / IBI after tIDLE / tAVAL respectively.

fsm_states.name: START_DETECT
fsm_states.description: Either Master or (in IBI / Hot-Join / Secondary Master Request from Bus Available) Slave drives SDA HIGH→LOW while SCL HIGH → bus becomes busy.

fsm_states.name: ADDR_HDR_ARBITRABLE
fsm_states.description: Address Header following a START — driven Open-Drain initially; Open-Drain bit-by-bit arbitration on SDA; may transition to Push-Pull mid-header per Section 5.1.2.2.2 (optimization).

fsm_states.name: ADDR_HDR_PUSH_PULL
fsm_states.description: Address Header following a Repeated START — driven entirely Push-Pull except the 9th ACK/NACK bit (Open-Drain).

fsm_states.name: ADDR_ACK_WAIT
fsm_states.description: 9th SCL bit of address header: addressed Slave drives SDA LOW = ACK; HIGH = NACK (Open-Drain).

fsm_states.name: WRITE_DATA_WORD
fsm_states.description: Master drives 8 data bits Push-Pull MSb-first, then drives T-Bit = odd parity = XOR(Data[7:0], 1) on 9th SCL bit.

fsm_states.name: READ_DATA_WORD
fsm_states.description: Slave drives 8 data bits Push-Pull MSb-first, then drives T-Bit on 9th SCL bit: T=1 continue, T=0 end-of-message.

fsm_states.name: READ_DATA_PARK
fsm_states.description: On T=1, Slave releases SDA HIGH-Z on rising SCL — bus is 'parked' HIGH. Master may either let weak Pull-Up keep HIGH (continue) or drive SDA LOW (force Sr / abort).

fsm_states.name: DAA_ENTDAA
fsm_states.description: Master broadcasts ENTDAA (0x07) → Sr + 7'h7E + R + ACK → slaves drive 48-bit PID + BCR + DCR onto SDA; Master clocks SCL only; Open-Drain arbitration; lowest concatenated value wins.

fsm_states.name: DAA_ADDR_ASSIGN
fsm_states.description: Master drives 7-bit Dynamic Address + 1-bit odd-parity on SDA Open-Drain; winning slave ACKs on the next SCL bit.

fsm_states.name: DAA_REPEAT
fsm_states.description: After ACK, Master returns to Sr + 7'h7E + R until no slave ACKs; then issues STOP.

fsm_states.name: IBI_ARBITRATION
fsm_states.description: From Bus Available Condition, Slave pulls SDA LOW; Master drives SCL; Slave drives its Dynamic Address (RnW=1) Open-Drain; lower address wins.

fsm_states.name: IBI_ACK_DECIDE
fsm_states.description: Master decides to ACK (accept) or NACK (reject) the IBI; if ACK and BCR[2]=1, Slave sends one or more Mandatory Data Bytes with T-Bit continuation.

fsm_states.name: HOTJOIN_REQUEST
fsm_states.description: From Bus Idle Condition (≥ tIDLE), Hot-Join Slave drives Hot-Join Address 7'h02 (RnW=0); Master may NACK (try later), ACK + DISHJ, or ACK + ENTDAA.

fsm_states.name: SECMASTER_REQUEST
fsm_states.description: BCR-marked Secondary Master drives its own Dynamic Address (RnW=0) in arbitrable header → Master responds; handoff finalized via GETACCMST (0x91).

fsm_states.name: MASTER_CLOCK_STALL
fsm_states.description: Master holds SCL LOW under specific transitory conditions (ACK/NACK Phase, Write Parity Bit, T-Bit before Sr/STOP/next-read, DAA first bit). See Table 11.

fsm_states.name: HDR_EXIT_DETECT
fsm_states.description: Every device watches SDA toggles while SCL stays LOW; defined HDR Exit Pattern returns the bus to SDR Mode.

fsm_states.name: STOP_GENERATE
fsm_states.description: Master drives SDA LOW→HIGH while SCL HIGH → frame ends; bus becomes Free after tCAS / tBUF.

fsm_hints.trigger: Either Master starts a frame from Bus Free / Available, or Slave starts a request (IBI / Hot-Join / Secondary Master Request) from Bus Available / Bus Idle.
fsm_hints.rule: Address Header has 9 SCL bits; SDR Data Word has 9 SCL bits (8 data + 1 T-Bit). On Push-Pull SDA, only one driver may be active. Slave NEVER drives SCL.
fsm_hints.abort: Master may abort a Slave-driven read at T-Bit HIGH by issuing Repeated START; or end any transaction with STOP.

anti_deadlock_rule: Slaves cannot clock-stretch SCL; the only path through which a Slave delays the Master is the T-Bit end-of-message mechanism, Master Clock Stall (controlled by Master), and Open-Drain arbitration. SCL is always driven by the Master.
exit_from_reset: After POR every I3C device releases SDA and SCL HIGH-Z (Failsafe pads if Hot-Join). Main Master enters Dynamic Address Assignment Mode after collecting static-address / LVR data for any Legacy I2C devices and SETDASA / SETAASA for known-static I3C devices, then issues ENTDAA (0x07) to assign Dynamic Addresses to all remaining I3C devices.

default_ready_state_recommendation.SDA_idle: HIGH (released by all devices; optional High-Keeper).
default_ready_state_recommendation.header_ack_window: Slave pulls SDA LOW only during the 9th SCL bit of the address header (Open-Drain).
default_ready_state_recommendation.data_t_bit_window: Master-write: Master drives T-Bit on the 9th SCL bit. Slave-read: Slave drives T-Bit on the 9th SCL bit; on T=1 it releases SDA HIGH-Z to allow Master abort.
default_ready_state_recommendation.no_slave_clock_stretch: Slave-side SCL stretching is forbidden — must NOT pull SCL LOW.

channel_dependency_rules_master.note: Master drives SCL Push-Pull (or Open-Drain in legacy / arbitration); generates START / STOP / Sr / DAA-assigned addresses; in Master-write drives SDA Push-Pull for data and T-Bit; in Master-read releases SDA after the address header. May Master Clock Stall under specific transitory conditions (Table 11).

channel_dependency_rules_slave.note: Slave samples SDA on rising SCL; drives SDA only during ACK windows, Slave-read data bytes + T-Bit, IBI arbitration, ENTDAA payload (PID/BCR/DCR), Hot-Join address. NEVER drives SCL.

arbitration_rule: Open-Drain wired-AND on SDA, MSb-first: the device that drives LOW wins. Used in (a) arbitrable address header after S, (b) IBI address contention, (c) ENTDAA Provisional ID stream — the lowest concatenated value wins.
synchronization_rule: Single Master drives SCL Push-Pull; no SCL synchronization mechanism is required because slaves cannot stretch SCL. During Master handoff to a Secondary Master, the two Masters overlap their drive for at least tMMOverlap before the new Master takes sole control.
master_clock_stall_conditions_table11: ACK/NACK Phase — Master may stall SCL LOW to delay accepting an IBI / decision.
Write Parity Bit — Master may stall before driving T-Bit on a Master-write byte.
T-Bit before next Read Data — Master may stall to slow down the Slave's next read word.
T-Bit before STOP — Master may stall before issuing STOP to give Slave time to release SDA.
T-Bit before Repeated START — Master may stall before Sr.
Dynamic Address First Bit — Master may stall in DAA between PID streams and address assignment.
